reason: Concrete counterexample to the claimed Neumann bound as written: take the exact scalar C*-algebra X=C (epsilon_r=0, J=1) and V=sqrt(3/2). For r=1/4, V has a right inverse and |V^dagger V-J|=1/2=2r, so V lies in calUbar_r. But L_{V^dagger}L_V-I is multiplication by |V|^2-1=1/2, hence its operator norm is 1/2, not <=1/4. Decreasing the root guard C_pol*(epsilon_r+delta)<=kappa_pol cannot fix this because the node assumes only r<=1/4 and does not relate r to delta. The intended applications appear to need the missing hypothesis r<=c*delta (or a separately sufficiently small r).
